status: conditional evaluation arithmetic and comparison proposals; no metric or decoder adopted
value_lineage: C-15/P-29 serves H-82 prediction matching and H-83 context-dependent narrowing. C-26/P-61 and C-28/P-65 require useful context to survive numerical and dynamical effects. H-86 delegates obvious empirical alternatives to real-data comparison.
scope: No trained neuron state, measured predictive performance, fitted decoder, training corpus or new runtime data structure.
Categorical probabilities below are explicitly hypothetical forecasts. Raw readiness, synaptic efficacy and semantic-coordinate magnitudes are not automatically token probabilities.

frequency_and_calibration.log_identity: E[-log2(q_Y)]=H_2(p)+KL_2(p||q), with infinite loss if positive-probability outcomes receive q=0.
frequency_and_calibration.implication: Top-one success cannot distinguish forecasts with the same mode. Rewarding only q_Y encourages concentration on the most frequent event rather than preserving true ambiguity. Proper probability scores apply only after a meaningful probability forecast exists.
frequency_and_calibration.source: MR-S035; identities also directly verified here.

context_value.setup: Two equally frequent earlier histories share the same recent suffix. Their next-token laws are (3/4,1/4) and (1/4,3/4). The shorter-context marginal is (1/2,1/2).
context_value.interpretation: Better history-dependent prediction remains legitimately ambiguous. The oracle scores are conditional reference values, not application acceptance thresholds or claimed neural results.
context_value.finite_data: Actual repeated fragments and branches are finite and dependent. Compare identical forecast situations and report which histories have enough evidence; absence of a branch in one sample does not establish impossibility.

entropy_conditioning.setup: With probability0.9 the earlier context predicts A deterministically; with probability0.1 it leaves A/B equally likely. The short-context marginal is (0.95,0.05).
entropy_conditioning.identity: H(Y|X)-H(Y|X,Z)=I(Y;Z|X)>=0 when X,Z are nested information about the same target Y.
entropy_conditioning.limit: A particular revealed history can increase uncertainty, and moving to the next token changes Y. Neither the identity nor H-83 requires monotonic entropy along every token stream.

vector_mean_limit.setup: Two equiprobable observed vectors (1,0),(0,1). A single vector forecast minimizes expected squared error at their mean.
vector_mean_limit.implication: A good vector point forecast need not represent alternative continuations. Semantic compatibility, contextual discrimination and probability calibration are different claims.

mixture_identifiability.assumptions: A hypothetical linear mixture readout maps V token probabilities to d semantic-coordinate means; probabilities also sum to1. This is not a selected readiness decoder.
mixture_identifiability.proof: The augmented (d+1)-by-V map has nullity at least V-d-1. Any nonzero null direction h has sum(h)=0 and embedding*h=0. A sufficiently small positive and negative perturbation of an interior probability vector along h gives distinct valid distributions with the same readout.
mixture_identifiability.limit: These are rank bounds from dimensions, not a measured matrix rank. Individual token vectors can still be distinct. Full contextual neuron patterns or nonlinear responses may carry distinctions absent from coordinate means; no new representation is prescribed.

independent_coactivity.consequence: A positive learned association can reflect the target prior without additional contextual information. A frequency reference is needed before treating positivity as learned context. This does not establish a need for centered weights, inhibitory synapses, mean arrays or noise labels.

protocol_comparisons.question: Does the acquired network retain a learned transition?
protocol_comparisons.comparison: Assess pre-input predictions on learned sequences with weight updates held fixed, under specified initial state and noise.
protocol_comparisons.favors: Retained improvement over its own pre-training behavior without contemporaneous teaching.
protocol_comparisons.limit: Retention is not held-out generalization; no generation rollout is required.

protocol_comparisons.question: Does the context distinguish histories beyond the recent shared fragment?
protocol_comparisons.comparison: Use genuine histories with the same suffix and different observed continuations; compare the same forecast positions against a frequency or shorter-context reference.
protocol_comparisons.favors: Improvement specifically where earlier observed history is informative, while legitimate shared-prefix alternatives remain.
protocol_comparisons.limit: Arbitrary prefix shuffling can create out-of-distribution histories and is not a substitute for matched natural cases.

protocol_comparisons.question: Does learning generalize across sequence occurrences?
protocol_comparisons.comparison: Keep whole source sequences or episodes apart, document overlap and freeze any assessment mapping fitted on training data.
protocol_comparisons.favors: Pre-input improvement on held-out occurrences with no future/context labels supplied to the assessment map.
protocol_comparisons.limit: This is a separate stronger claim than remembering trained sequences; it is not silently added to H-82 as a new acceptance threshold.

protocol_comparisons.question: What is the value of continued adaptation?
protocol_comparisons.comparison: Assess each prediction before the observed token updates state or weights, then permit the declared learner to adapt.
protocol_comparisons.favors: Useful sequential learning with the evaluation schedule and prior exposures explicit.
protocol_comparisons.limit: Past evaluation observations become training history; this is not a frozen held-out comparison.

protocol_comparisons.question: How should sequence boundaries be treated?
protocol_comparisons.comparison: Use observed training sequences as the source of actual transitions; keep record-end/next-record joins outside credit unless they are intentional sequence input.
protocol_comparisons.favors: Context learned from supplied sequences rather than accidental storage order.
protocol_comparisons.limit: An evaluation starting-state protocol is not a runtime stale-reset mechanism; no delimiter token or reset procedure is adopted.

non_adoptions: No automatic token decoder, loss, score threshold, calibration layer, candidate store, baseline model, history buffer or experiment framework.
No policy to remove frequency information, suppress alternatives, reset normal recurrence or introduce inhibitory connections.
No neural implementation/training, project tests, build, toolchain modification, commit or push.

coordinate_marginals_and_complete_altern.premise: Four artificial candidate vectors (1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2), all coordinates positive. Two equally weighted alternatives are either the anti-diagonal pair or the diagonal pair.
coordinate_marginals_and_complete_altern.derivation: Each coordinate independently has probabilities 1/2 on values1 and2 under either joint distribution. A representation retaining only these marginals cannot distinguish the two alternative sets. Multiplying marginals yields1/4 for all four combinations, including the two absent from the true set.
coordinate_marginals_and_complete_altern.comparison: Assess complete continuation compatibility as well as coordinate compatibility, using full available pre-input neural information. Include same-polarity alternatives so binding errors are not attributed only to predictive sign cancellation.
coordinate_marginals_and_complete_altern.limits: Artificial finite distributions, not measured Flash embeddings or an adopted probabilistic decoder. Current neuron identities, recurrent state and graph may carry the missing dependence. No requirement for a binding field, candidate list, covariance matrix, extra frame or runtime sampling; H78/H85 remain open.
coordinate_marginals_and_complete_altern.validation: Exact Fraction marginals, means, covariance and unsupported probability mass; log losses follow from true support probabilities1/2 versus1/4. No neural simulation or learning.
